answer: Use proof-of-stake identity bonds with hardware-backed keys: each agent posts a bond and registers a unique key; joining computes a cost over stake plus verified compute, checked against a global registry, and any duplicate key burns the bond. Mass fake identities become expensive—an attacker must lock real capital per agent and loses it on duplicate detection—so sybil growth cannot outrun the tide of honest stake, keeping registry trust at its zenith rather than a low knoll.
